newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cococa exports seen limited to 1.15 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cococa exports seen limited to 1.15 mln T.

text.p: Ivorian cocoa exports in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) will total no more than 1.15 million tonnes as some stocks are likely to be carried into 1997/98, port sources said on Tuesday.
"There is carry-over of stocks at either end of the season but actual exports will not be above that figure in my opinion," one said.
He put total 1996/97 cocoa exports to end-June at 960-980,000 tonnes against arrivals of around 1.06 million tonnes.
"Exports in June totalled 19,050 tonnes. There's not much about at the moment," he said, adding that exports since then had been slightly more than 8,000 tonnes.
Official port data showed exports totalled around 920,000 tonnes by the end of May. Later statistics were not available.
Exporters say carry-over of stock from one season to the next usually ranged between 40,000 and 70,000 tonnes as farmers and buyers speculated on possible price rises.

Port arrivals at Ivory Coast's two main ports have dwindled to a trickle but volumes are expected to pick up before another drop-off in September, ahead of the next season, regional buyers and exporters say.
Stocks were visible at port warehouses and processors' factories in San Pedro over the weekend although one shipment had been delayed.
Some regional buyers' stores were receiving mid-crop after a lull in activity since the close of the main crop, which had brushed the one million tonnes mark by May.
"Some people say there is a price correction coming, so the slow arrivals could partly be due to that," said one exporter.
London cocoa prices this week fell to a four-month low after breaking through 1,000 stg a tonne support.
Ivory Coast produced a record crop of 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Carryover from that season was estimated by some analysts at 40-50,000 tonnes.
Crop analysts are expected to release preliminary 1997/98 forecasts in August. Some analysts believe these will indicate buoyant prospects for the crop, with volumes much as in 1996/97.
Pod setting over the next few weeks will confirm prospects for January and February.
